findings.title: Storage failures recorded as legacy duration metrics
findings.body: When Storage.Create fails (line 45) and when Storage.Update fails (line 129), the code calls recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration. Unified-storage errors are therefore attributed to the legacy metrics, and the storage error metrics miss them.

findings.title: Async legacy DeleteCollection recorded as storage duration
findings.body: The goroutine that calls Legacy.DeleteCollection records its outcome with recordStorageDuration. It should use recordLegacyDuration, so the legacy metric is never emitted for delete-collection and the storage metric is polluted.

findings.title: Delete success metric uses name as the kind label
findings.body: On successful delete, recordStorageDuration is passed `name` where every other call passes options.Kind. This creates a high-cardinality label series per object name and splits the metrics for this method.

findings.title: Delete stores the wrong logger in the context
findings.body: klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log) is used instead of the enriched `log`. The method, name and kind values are lost for downstream logging, and the async legacy goroutine inherits this context.

findings.title: Async legacy write reuses the request context
findings.body: The goroutines derive their context from the request ctx. Once the HTTP request completes, that ctx is cancelled, so the legacy create/update/delete may be cancelled mid-flight or fail immediately. The legacy write is not reliable. Use context.WithoutCancel(ctx), or a background context that carries the logger, for the legacy write. Update's goroutine also reuses objInfo and the validation closures after the request has returned, and legacy failures are only recorded in metrics, not logged.

findings.title: Tests don't verify async legacy writes
findings.body: The tests never wait for or assert that the legacy mock is called after the unified write. The legacy mocks are set up but unverified, and the goroutines may outlive the test or race with mock state. The error case sets up a Legacy Create expectation that is never used.
